title: Pennsylvania Reports Ninth Measles Death of 2026 as U.S. Tally Reaches 13
excerpt: Pennsylvania reported its ninth measles-associated death of 2026 on Monday, bringing the state-reported U.S. tally to 13.
content:
Pennsylvania reported its ninth measles-associated death of 2026 on Monday, Nov. 23, bringing the number of measles deaths reported by states this year to 13 — more than double the six the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has confirmed.

The person who died was an unvaccinated resident of Centre County who tested positive for measles, the Pennsylvania Department of Health said. No further identifying details were released, to protect the family's privacy. Pennsylvania's totals as of Nov. 23: 1,638 confirmed cases, 46 counties, 330 hospitalizations and nine deaths, with 49 newly confirmed cases since Nov. 18. Only five cases — less than 1% — were among vaccinated people. The nine deaths, by county of residence: Centre one, Clinton one, Jefferson two, Lancaster three, Mifflin one and Montour one. All nine deaths were in people who were unvaccinated or too young to be vaccinated, according to the department.

Virginia announced its first measles-associated death of 2026 on Friday, Nov. 20 — a young child aged 0 to 4 who tested positive for measles. It was Virginia's first measles-related death since 1978. Virginia had 220 cases in 2026 as of Nov. 19, mostly in central Virginia, with 195 cases there; 18% of the state's cases were in children 0 to 4.

The state-reported national total is now 13 measles-associated deaths in 2026: nine in Pennsylvania, two in Wisconsin, one in New York and one in Virginia. The CDC has confirmed six deaths in 2026, without naming states, and says the number is subject to change as it works with the Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists on a standardized measles-death case definition. The gap arose after the CDC began using National Center for Health Statistics mortality data instead of state figures, according to Reuters. The CDC's national case count stands at 5,838 confirmed cases in 2026 as of Nov. 19, across 47 jurisdictions, with 96% linked to outbreaks and 43 outbreaks this year. The 426 new cases confirmed in the week before Nov. 19 were the largest one-week jump in decades.

The U.S. officially lost measles elimination status on Nov. 17, 2026, when the Pan American Health Organization determined the virus had circulated continuously for at least 12 months. The U.S. had held the status since 2000. Mexico and Bolivia lost it the same day. To regain it, the U.S. must submit a corrective action plan and prove 12 months free of the virus. Webb Watch reported the loss of elimination status on Nov. 14 and Nov. 19.

The Virginia Department of Health said that “although anyone can become seriously ill, children younger than five years old, pregnant people, and people with weakened immune systems are at increased risk of complications.” CDC Director Dr. Erica Schwartz said: “The measles elimination designation is not what protects Americans. Vaccination does.”
